PullRequest.Title: artifacts: Connect the agent host, extension API, and agent tools
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Connect the shared runtime to Agent Host sessions and independently contributed extensions.

- Add the proposed `chatArtifactIntegrations` API, activation/registration plumbing, and typed main-thread/extension-host bridge.
- Negotiate host capabilities, compose host and client integrations without changing their authority, and retain startup/reconnect behavior.
- Preserve trusted artifact origin, durable notices, queued/live/restored action snapshots, and advertised chat ownership, including opaque remote chat identifiers.
- Add deferred `get_artifact_status`, `run_artifact_action`, `set_artifact_automation`, and `disable_artifact_automation` tools, with turn-provenance checks and explicit in-chat confirmation.
- Let the host use client integrations without forwarding extension credentials or allowing recursive client prompt execution.

The eager tool budget is unchanged. The generic renderer and built-in GitHub implementation are deliberately left to later layers.

## Stack

This is **2 of 4**, based on #343002, not directly on `main`.

| Order | PR | Base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #343002 - Shared integration runtime | `main` |
| 2 | **#343001 - Agent host, extension API, and agent tools (this PR)** | #343002 |
| 3 | #343003 - Generic artifact UI | #343001 |
| 4 | #343000 - GitHub pull request integration | #343003 |

Part of the replacement stack for #337678 and #338107. Extension consumers, including the separate ExP extension, remain outside this repository's PR stack.

## Validation

- `npm run valid-layers-check` - **passed**.
- `git --no-pager diff --name-only HEAD -- '*.ts' | xargs ./node_modules/.bin/eslint --quiet` - **passed**, run before committing this slice.
- `git diff --cached --check` - **passed** before committing.
- Bridge, provenance, tool-budget, and lifecycle tests - **303 passed**:

The proposed API declaration was also checked byte-for-byte against the separate ExP consumer. No live prompts, external mutations, or consent changes were made during validation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path is explicit: `$createIntegration` cannot return until the loop completes, `convertDetails` maps every fact and item, and `ExtensionArtifactDetails` unconditionally issues a second `$acquireDetails` RPC. The API places no item-count bound on a details snapshot, so only the real-world payload size is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: extension provider detail models, serialized IPC bytes, and allocated fact/item DTO objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is O(number of advertised details IDs × facts/items per details snapshot) for each integration creation, and can be multiplied by up to 20 artifacts in the new list-status path.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased latency and CPU/GC pressure from unnecessary extension-host serialization
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no extension artifact-integration bridge and therefore no eager detail construction or duplicate details IPC on artifact acquisition.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Creating an extension-backed artifact integration now eagerly constructs and serializes every advertised details model before the artifact model can finish initializing; actual details access then acquires the same details a second time to establish the live handle.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 166-182 make `$createIntegration` synchronously iterate every main/section/list details ID, call `integration.acquireDetails`, convert the complete details payload, and include it in the creation response. The newly added main-thread `ExtensionArtifactDetails` constructor later always calls `$acquireDetails` again when the details are actually acquired.
Findings.Title: Acquire extension artifact details lazily
Findings.Impact: An artifact with several or large details lists delays model creation and the agent status critical path while the extension host allocates and serializes data that may never be requested. With status listing, this can occur for up to 20 artifacts at once, causing IPC payload growth, CPU/GC pressure, and visible tool latency.
Findings.Evidence: `ExtHostChatArtifactIntegrations.$createIntegration` loops over all details IDs at lines 167-181 and calls provider `acquireDetails` plus `convertDetails`; `convertDetails` maps the full `facts` and `items` arrays. On first consumer access, `ExtensionArtifactResource.acquireDetails` creates `ExtensionArtifactDetails`, whose constructor unconditionally invokes `proxy.$acquireDetails`, so the eager snapshot does not replace the normal acquisition/subscription. This path is reached by agent artifact acquisition and is multiplied when status listing acquires several artifacts.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep `$createIntegration` limited to state and action descriptors, then acquire details only when a consumer requests a details ID. If an initial snapshot is required, retain the created details model/handle and reuse it for updates instead of disposing it and issuing `$acquireDetails` again.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The 20-way scheduling is explicit in the changed `Promise.all`. Tracing `acquireArtifact` shows cold model creation iterates registered integrations, client composition can issue one reverse AHP request per artifact, and extension integrations cross main-thread/extension-host RPC for matching and creation. Resource pools coalesce creation only after matching and only for identical canonical resources; they do not bound aggregate calls. Exact provider/network duration is the remaining magnitude uncertainty.
Findings.PerformanceResource: AHP reverse requests, main-thread/extension-host RPC calls, provider model creation, and possible provider network requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Aggregate concurrency grows linearly with recorded artifacts up to 20; each artifact checks registered integrations, while only identical post-match resources can share creation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: burst IPC/network load, contention, and reduced throughput during artifact status listing
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no `get_artifact_status` list operation and therefore no multi-artifact acquisition burst on an agent tool call.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new status-list operation launches every selected artifact acquisition concurrently rather than applying any shared concurrency limit or backpressure.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 348 wraps all `recorded.slice(0, MAX_LISTED_ARTIFACTS)` acquisitions in one `Promise.all`, immediately starting up to 20 `accessor.acquireArtifact` calls for a single omitted-argument `get_artifact_status` invocation.
Findings.Title: Bound status-list artifact acquisition concurrency
Findings.Impact: A session with 20 recorded links can create a 20-request AHP/extension-host burst and up to 20 simultaneous provider match/create operations, increasing tool latency through contention and risking remote API throttling for integrations that load live status.
Findings.Evidence: `listStatus` starts up to `MAX_LISTED_ARTIFACTS` (20) acquisitions in one `Promise.all`. `acquireComposedArtifact` may add a client acquisition after the host model, `ClientArtifactIntegrationEndpoint` relays that over reverse RPC, and `ArtifactModel.refresh` invokes every registered integration's match/create path. The registry pools identical matched resources but performs matching per artifact and has no global limiter; references are released after each summary, so ordinary cold listings repeat this work.
Findings.Recommendation: Process the selected artifacts through a small shared concurrency limiter while preserving result order and the existing 20-artifact output cap; keep model/resource coalescing intact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent calls get_artifact_status without an artifact to list integrated recorded artifacts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool waits for every selected acquisition and its settled summary before returning JSON to the agent; all work is on the tool-call critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire and observe a client-coordinated artifact through reverse AHP RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 20 concurrent artifact acquisitions per tool call; one client acquisition per artifact when a client is selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact status-list tool or multi-artifact bridge acquisition existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Promise.all waits for the slowest acquisition/summary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Match and create extension-backed integrations across the main-thread/extension-host bridge
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Each cold artifact checks registered integrations; up to 20 artifacts are active concurrently. Canonical resource creation may coalesce only after each match completes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No extension artifact integration API bridge existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model initialization waits for provider matching and creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider-defined live artifact matching/model creation may access an external service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Provider dependent; aggregate concurrency can reach the 20 selected artifacts, while integrations are attempted sequentially within each artifact model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This agent tool did not invoke artifact providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Any provider latency contributes to the slowest Promise.all member and can contend or throttle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Recorded artifacts with links/URIs, capped at 20 after newest-first selection; registered integrations multiply matching work after cache/coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all creates up to 20 concurrent artifact acquisitions with no shared limiter. Each artifact's integrations initialize sequentially; aggregate cross-artifact concurrency remains up to 20.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A live model is coalesced by session/artifact while referenced or retained by automation. Ordinary list references are released after summary, so later cold list calls rematch. Resource creation can coalesce by canonical key only after match and only while referenced; negative matches are not retained across released models.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the Promise.all cardinality and transitive AHP/extension-host paths are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count, provider network behavior, and typical artifact count vary, but the 20-way IPC/provider burst is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable concurrency burst; submitted a medium-severity finding recommending bounded parallelism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or acquire an extension-backed artifact model, including a single-artifact status read
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Integration creation waits for `$createIntegration`; normal status additionally waits for requested details before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return integration state plus eager snapshots for every advertised details ID from extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One creation RPC per matching extension/artifact, containing every main/section/list details snapshot and every fact/item in those snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No extension integration bridge or eager details payload existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The creation response cannot complete until all details models are acquired, converted, and serialized.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the requested details again to establish a live details handle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional RPC for each details ID actually consumed, even if its eager snapshot was included in creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No duplicate details acquisition path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Actual details observation repeats provider acquisition and serialization work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Advertised details IDs and the unbounded facts/items supplied by each extension details model; multi-artifact status listing multiplies this per artifact.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All details IDs are processed synchronously during each extension creation; multiple artifact creations can execute concurrently through the list path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The eager details models are disposed immediately, so their provider resources are not retained for the later live acquisition. The copied initial DTO is cached on the main thread but does not suppress the second RPC.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both acquisitions and full-array conversion are explicit in changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension detail sizes vary, but the eager all-details traversal and duplicate acquisition are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager serialization/repeated work; submitted a medium-severity finding to make details lazy or reuse retained handles.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent reads or changes one artifact, runs a native action, or changes automation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One artifact acquisition precedes status/action/configuration work; native actions may wait up to 60 seconds for settlement and automation enablement waits for explicit in-chat confirmation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire host and optionally selected-client artifact models
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host acquisition and at most one selected-client acquisition per tool call; client acquisition is attempted after the host model and bounded to 10 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Artifact integration tools did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both acquisitions are on the tool critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke provider native action or update provider automation configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected integration/action or sequential configuration per matching contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The tool waits for configuration completion or bounded run status.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single recorded artifact, its registered integrations, and selected automation options.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Integrations initialize sequentially within the model; action invocation is singular. Disable-all automation configures matching contributions sequentially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session/artifact models are reused while referenced or retained by enabled automation; cold calls recreate and rematch. Run snapshots are capped at 50.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and bounds.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider execution time is external and varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond eager extension details; waits and ordering are bounded and required by action/consent semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent host startup restores durable artifact automation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The bootstrap starts restoration with `void`; work is off the agent-host startup completion path, though restored automation availability waits for it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One memoized ledger read per host runtime cold start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact automation ledger was initialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the main host startup critical path due to the unawaited initialize call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recreate provider bindings retained by enabled automation or unsettled runs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquisition per retained binding, processed sequentially after the ledger read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays only restoration of those automations, not host startup completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted bindings that still have enabled automation or unsettled/indeterminate runs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Restoration is sequential, preventing a provider/network burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Initialization is memoized; restored models stay retained only while automation or unsettled work requires them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for placement, memoization, and sequential behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Number of durable enabled automations is user dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup regression because the filesystem/provider work is off the startup critical path and bounded by retained automation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect/reconnect an agent host and advertise client extension integrations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session-change handling constructs the coordinator synchronously, while Web Lock/IndexedDB setup and extension activation proceed asynchronously; reconnect reoffers the catalog before host use.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/read the local IndexedDB artifact ledger under a Web Lock
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local coordinator per profile/target-host scope, shared across windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No local artifact coordinator was created.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and not awaited by session refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One activation request per new connection/runtime; the extension service coalesces already-active extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent-host connection did not activate artifact integration extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by session refresh, but required before the full catalog can be advertised.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Offer descriptors and relay updates between client and host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalog offer per connection/catalog change; updates follow integration events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No client integration offer protocol existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog offers are asynchronous and do not block connection completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Connections/reconnections, profiles, and registered extension integrations (host accepts at most 100 offered descriptors per client).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single selected registration is active; older registrations are inert and per-connection servers are disposed on reconnect.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Coordinator selection is stored per profile/target host; IndexedDB persists the ledger; extension activation is naturally warm after first activation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lifecycle and off-critical-path scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension activation cost varies by installed extension.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: eager activation is intentional for pre-recording catalog discovery, is asynchronous, and is coalesced per connection/runtime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore and render artifact-initiated chat turns and notices
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat/session restoration maps metadata while rebuilding existing request/response models; rendering reads small validated metadata fields.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of restored chat turns and notices.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing restoration sequencing is unchanged; the diff adds constant-size metadata parsing per request/notice.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Metadata is persisted with the chat model and restored from existing session data; no new cache or remote fetch is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changes are metadata pass-through and icon selection only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Chat history length varies, but added work is constant per restored turn.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispatch and track background artifact prompts/actions through live chats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A dispatch waits for its matching acknowledgement or a 30-second timeout; chat observation subscribes only for the handle lifetime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one chat action over the agent-host protocol and await its acknowledgement
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per artifact prompt transition/cancellation, with correlation by client sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The artifact run waits for acknowledgement; ambiguous disconnects fail rather than replay.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each dispatch has its own listener/timer; integration runtime sequencing and provider rules govern run concurrency rather than an unbounded batch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat subscriptions and request correlation state are retained only while observations/handles live and are cleared on disposal or disconnect.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for timeout and cleanup ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Concurrent automation count depends on enabled user rules.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: lifecycle cleanup and no-replay semantics bound retained listeners and work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 89 changed files, tracing startup, connection/reconnect, extension-host bridging, tool execution, background actions, persistence, and chat restoration. Submitted two medium-confidence/high-mechanism findings: eager duplicate details serialization and unbounded-at-20 concurrent status-list acquisition.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
